craft_claim: Irreverent prose amuses only when its violation of a sacred or self-important register is appraised as safe; the same gesture reads as offense when the violation appraises as real harm or genuine contempt.

supporting_evidence.note: Amusement follows violations that are simultaneously seen as benign; the three benignity conditions are an alternative norm suggesting acceptability, weak commitment to the violated norm, and psychological distance from the violation.

The Semantic-Script Theory of Humor explains how a single situation can be read through two incompatible scripts at once — the formal counterpart of a violation landing inside a recognized comic reading rather than a hostile one.

counterevidence.note: The benign-violation account is a general humor theory tested in the moral domain, not a study of irreverent prose; it is adjacent evidence and the claim is scoped to reader appraisal of register-violation.
Negativity bias (negative potency, negativity dominance) means a failed appraisal weighs more than the comic gain: once the violation reads as genuinely harmful, that reading dominates the amusement.

scope: Deflation of pomp, ceremony, and piety-as-performance inside frames readers treat as sanctioned or low-stakes (parody, deadpan narration, established comic personas).
exceptions: When the target is a real person or vulnerable group, audiences appraise the same machinery as harm rather than safety — that boundary is covered by clm-tone-irreverent-prejudiced-norm-backfire.
Appraisals are audience-relative: what one readership holds weakly (or distances from) another holds as sacred.
